bull.b: ACI-7104 has generated durable clinical and biological validation in early Parkinson’s disease, with sustained safety, immunogenicity, cerebrospinal-fluid penetration and target-engagement signals. These results support advancing the program into an expanded efficacy-focused phase and strengthen the potential value of AC Immune’s proprietary pipeline.

FDA Fast Track status and IND clearance reduce regulatory friction and allow broader U.S. clinical execution for ACI-7104. This strengthens the program’s development infrastructure, may improve access to regulatory interaction, and could increase strategic interest in AC Immune’s Parkinson’s franchise.

ACI-19764 adds a second wholly owned clinical program with a differentiated oral, brain-penetrant mechanism and encouraging early pharmacology. Positive Phase 1/1b findings broaden AC Immune’s opportunity set beyond one lead asset and provide additional potential catalysts across neurological and inflammatory diseases.

bear.b: Large recurring operating and net losses, combined with volatile and declining revenue, show that AC Immune has not yet achieved operating leverage. The expense base remains substantial relative to revenue, so clinical progress has yet to translate into internally funded profitability or a stable earnings foundation.

The return to heavy cash consumption increases dependence on financing, partnerships, or milestone receipts to sustain clinical development. Even though cash flow tracked losses closely, the negative current run-rate limits flexibility and makes continued pipeline investment more sensitive to funding availability.

A materially smaller equity base reflects the cumulative effect of ongoing losses and reduces the balance-sheet cushion available to support long development timelines. Low debt limits immediate leverage pressure, but declining equity leaves less capacity to absorb setbacks or fund programs without further capital actions.
